end.summary:
Distinguished observation, hypothesis, law and theory using examples.
Identified testing and measurement as parts of investigating a claim.
Correctly described salt water boiling at a higher temperature than plain water in the example.
Explained theory as an explanation, but said theories turn into laws when proven.
Teach-back was not passed; the theory-versus-law distinction remained mixed up.
end.parentNote: Tara practised sorting scientific statements into observations, hypotheses, laws and theories, including a salt-water boiling-point example. They used testing, comparison and thermometer measurements to describe how a claim could be investigated. Tara still mixed up the idea that a theory becomes a law when proven; this was not corrected by the end of the lesson. At home, ask Tara to make two columns—“law describes a pattern” and “theory explains why”—and place one example in each.
